The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydroosmolarity of urine is controlled by the amount of calcium ion in the body, and the more calcium ion in the blood the greater the hydroosmolar response to antidiabetic hormone.

the calcium ion plays an important role in the mechanism of action of ADH in the toad bladder, and this role is probably related to the coupling of the hormonal stimulus with the cellular reabsorptive process.
